rules: Use simple, expressive TypeScript that is easy to read and maintain.
Prefer async/await over Promise chains.
Handle errors explicitly and provide informative error messages.
Document complex algorithms with clear explanations.
Utilize strong typing and avoid using 'any' type.
Use named exports over default exports for better refactoring support.
Follow consistent naming conventions across the codebase.
Organize imports with external libraries first, followed by internal modules.
Implement proper error handling for asynchronous operations.
Avoid deeply nested code blocks and prefer early returns.
Keep functions small and focused on a single responsibility.
Use camelCase for variables and functions, PascalCase for classes and interfaces.
Add appropriate JSDoc comments for public APIs.
Write defensive code that validates inputs and handles edge cases.
Ensure all UI elements are accessible according to WCAG standards.
Use CSS-in-JS or dedicated CSS modules to avoid styling conflicts.
Prefer composition over inheritance for code reuse.
Use dependency injection for better testability.
Implement proper resource cleanup in UI components and background services.
Keep the bundle size small by avoiding unnecessary dependencies.
Secure all communications with OpenRouter AI API using proper authentication.
Always respect user privacy and handle sensitive data with care.
Implement explicit user permission prompts for file system and command operations.
Design UI components with accessibility, responsiveness, and performance in mind.
Structure code to optimize for VS Code extension performance.
